recognize_zh: 密集的紅血球中散在數顆體積較大、染成藍灰紫色、缺乏中央淡染區的多染性紅血球（polychromatophilic cells），整體紅血球偏大，符合新生兒血液常見的多染性（polychromasia）。
features: Scattered larger red cells with bluish-gray to lilac cytoplasm (polychromatophilic cells)
Polychromatophilic cells lack central pallor and are larger than surrounding red cells
Background red cells relatively large with mild anisocytosis, fitting neonatal red cell indices
Occasional crenated red cells, likely artifact
Scattered platelets; no nucleated red cells or inclusions in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear from a neonate shows a crowded field of relatively large red cells with mild anisocytosis. Numerous scattered polychromatophilic red cells are present, appearing larger and bluish-gray without central pallor, reflecting residual RNA in reticulocytes. Occasional crenated cells are seen and platelets are present. Findings are consistent with polychromasia, which is physiologic in the newborn given the high reticulocyte count, but may be increased further in hemolysis (e.g. hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn).

ddx.vs: Spherocytes are small, dense and orange-pink without central pallor, whereas polychromatophilic cells are large and bluish.
A staining artifact colors all cells similarly, whereas true polychromasia affects individual larger cells that stain with new methylene blue as reticulocytes.
Basophilic stippling shows discrete blue dots within red cells, whereas polychromasia is diffuse blue-gray cytoplasmic tinting.
